blocks.text: Deco-Luxe is a mélange of Art Deco & Streamline Moderne revivals that emerged mainly in the mid 1970s, and peaked in the 1980s and early 1990s. It differs from the earlier Art Deco revival in the 1970s, Disco Deco, as it is more focused on the luxury side of Art Deco & the Roaring 20s, due to the rise of materialism and excess during the 1980s.

For the interior architectural style, it shifts into clear indulgence where rooms incorporate extended open layouts anchored by oversized, high-end leathers or curvaceous seating concealed in rich velvets. Symmetrical geometric patterns were applied for the flooring style flow, while soaring ceilings are often outfitted with custom lacquering, gold-leaf or recessed trays finishes to exaggerate the sense of scale.

For the exterior architecture, It leans on staggered, monumental, structures that have sleek curved corners influenced by the Streamline Moderne movement, drew inspiration from the ancient ziggurats, and relieved decorative panels. Buildings often place high-contrast structural framing, dramatic, exaggerated vertical piers, and chevron patterns etched into stone, metal grilles or stylized sunburst concrete.
Features rich materials such as chrome, lacquer, polished brass, mirrors, and glass.
Deep colors rely on white-and-black blocking, high-contrast palettes, or jewel tones such as emerald and gold paired with navy
Uses sleek lightning such as lamps with exposed bulbs, polished metal sconces, and dramatic glass fixtures.
Main elements feature sunbursts, bold geometries, zig-zags, clean symmetrical lines, and chevrons.
